name: Daily routine (dinacaryā)
method_summary: Rise at the brāhma muhūrta (before dawn) to protect life; attend to the body and cleanliness; clean the teeth with a twig suited to season and doṣa; apply collyrium to the eyes; nasal oil, gargling and (for some) medicated smoke; daily oil-massage, especially of head, ears and feet; exercise to half one's strength; bathing; clean clothes, fragrance; eat in measure when the previous meal is digested; follow good conduct through the day; at night, after a watch has passed, sleep remembering the gods, sages and teachers.

warnings.text: Tooth-twig, massage and bathing each have conditions in which they are to be avoided (indigestion, fever, eye and ear disease, kapha affliction, just after purification).

signs_of_progress: life, health, power and fame (AHS Sū 2.49)

name: Seasonal routine (ṛtucaryā)
method_summary: Adjust diet and conduct to the six seasons: in the 'taking' half (late winter to summer) strength declines and the dry tastes grow; in the 'releasing' half (rains to early winter) the moon restores strength; in winter the strong fire needs heavy, unctuous, sweet-sour-salt food; accumulated doṣas are cleared in the following season.

warnings.text: In winter the strong fire, finding no fuel, consumes the tissues; hence heavy food then (not a general licence).

name: Seasonal purification
method_summary: Removal of the doṣas accumulated in a season at its proper time (e.g. kapha of winter in spring), by the purificatory therapies, followed by rejuvenatives; purified doṣas do not recur. Summary only.

warnings.text: Doṣas that have accumulated too much, when provoked, can cut off life; doṣas merely subdued by fasting and digestives may flare again.

name: Oil massage (abhyaṅga)
method_summary: Daily anointing of the body with oil, especially head, ears and feet; it makes the body firm like an oiled pot or axle, calms vāta, improves skin, sight and sleep and delays ageing.

warnings.text: To be avoided by those afflicted with kapha, just after purificatory therapy, and with indigestion.

signs_of_progress: firmness, good skin, freedom from vāta-pain, good sleep (Ca Sū 5.86-89)

name: Exercise (vyāyāma)
method_summary: Bodily exertion for steadiness and strength, done in measure — to half one's strength by the strong in the cold season and spring, less at other times — followed by gentle massage.

warnings.text: Excess causes fatigue, wasting, thirst, bleeding disorders, cough, fever and vomiting; one who overdoes exercise, talk, travel, sex or waking perishes like a lion dragging an elephant.
To be avoided by the vāta- and pitta-afflicted, children, the old and those with indigestion.

signs_of_progress: lightness, capacity for work, kindled fire, reduced fat, firm well-divided limbs

name: Diet by measure, doṣa and quality
method_summary: Eat in the measure the fire can digest in due time; eat what is wholesome — what keeps balanced tissues balanced and restores the unbalanced — chosen by the twenty qualities (guṇa) and six tastes opposite to the provoked doṣa, and suited to constitution, season and habit; observe the eight factors (nature, preparation, combination, quantity, place, time, rules of eating, the eater); avoid incompatible foods. The mind's qualities also follow diet: the tāmasa and rājasa mental types are marked by greed for food.

warnings.text: Incompatible food (e.g. fish with milk) vitiates the blood and can be fatal; whatever provokes the doṣas without expelling them is unwholesome.

equivalents.note: the haṭha rule of measured, suitable food; Āyurveda gives its medical grounds (measure by the fire, wholesome and incompatible foods)

notes: 'Diet by guṇa' in Āyurveda means chiefly the twenty physical qualities; the Gītā's sāttvika/rājasa/tāmasa foods belong to U05.

name: Not suppressing the natural urges
method_summary: Do not hold back the arisen urges of urine, faeces, semen, flatus, vomiting, sneezing, belching, yawning, hunger, thirst, tears, sleep and breath after exertion; nor force them.

warnings.text: All diseases arise from forcing or suppressing the urges.

name: Keeping the three supports of life
method_summary: Right use of food, sleep and continence, by which the body is upheld as a house by its pillars.

name: Regimen of sleep
method_summary: Sleep at night; day-sleep is wholesome in summer and for the exhausted, weak, old, children and certain patients, but not for the fat, kapha-natured or those who eat unctuous food; induce sleep by massage, bathing, pleasant food and surroundings; drive away excess sleep by purification, fasting, anxiety and exercise.

warnings.text: Sleep untimely or in excess takes away happiness and life like another night of doom; day-sleep in the wrong season causes many kapha disorders.

name: Continence (brahmacarya)
method_summary: Lineage contribution (Āyurveda): the third support of life, 'the best of paths'; required of the medical student and of the one taking rejuvenation; sexual activity only in measure and at permitted times and places.

name: Good conduct (sadvṛtta)
method_summary: Follow, with constant mindfulness, the conduct of the good: honour gods, teachers and elders; keep clean; speak truly, gently and first; do not take or covet what is another's; restrain greed, envy, anger and pride; avoid the wicked and serve the elders; abandon the ten sinful acts; see all beings, even insects, as oneself; follow the middle way; reflect each night on how one's days are passing; be devoted to continence, knowledge, giving, friendliness, compassion, joy, equanimity and calm.
signs_of_progress: health and mastery of the senses at once (Ca Sū 8.18); a hundred years free of disease (8.31)

name: Rejuvenation by conduct (ācāra-rasāyana)
method_summary: Truthfulness, freedom from anger, abstinence from alcohol and sex, non-violence, calm, pleasant speech, recitation and purity, generosity, austerity, worship of gods and elders, compassion, balanced sleep, knowledge of place, time and measure, freedom from ego, inward-turned senses and study of dharma — by which one 'enjoys constant rasāyana'.

name: Rejuvenation therapy (rasāyana) — herbal
method_summary: Taken in youth or middle age after purification, by the self-controlled, either in a hut (kuṭīprāveśika) or amid ordinary life (vātātapika), with herbal preparations; its fruits are long life, memory, intelligence, health, youth, lustre and strength. No formulations recorded.

warnings.text: Rasāyana applied to an unpurified body is fruitless, like dye on a dirty cloth.
One who has not removed his bodily and mental doṣas never attains its benefits.
If disease arises from a lapse in the regimen, treat it with its own remedies, setting rasāyana aside.

prerequisites: purification of body; purity and restraint of mind (Ci 1.4.36-37)
signs_of_progress: long life, memory, intelligence, health, youth, lustre, voice, strength, success of speech (Ca Ci 1.1.7-8)

name: Hut-entering rejuvenation (kuṭīprāveśika)
method_summary: The principal mode of rasāyana: after preliminary rites, with shaved head, steadied resolve and a mind freed of its doṣas and turned to friendliness toward beings, the person enters a specially built secluded hut, is purified by cleansing therapies and then takes the rejuvenative under a physician's care. Summary only: construction, diet, preparations and durations are not recorded.

warnings.text: The better mode but very hard to carry out; only for the capable and self-controlled.
Diseases arising from lapses in the regimen are to be treated apart from the rasāyana.

prerequisites: capacity, health, wisdom, self-control, leisure and means (Ci 1.4.27)
notes: Marked restricted because the full regimen involves prolonged seclusion, purgation and special diet, and some formulations include metals and gems (e.g. Ci 1.4.22).

name: Intellect-promoting rejuvenatives
method_summary: Use of the medhya herbs — maṇḍūkaparṇī, liquorice, guḍūcī and above all śaṅkhapuṣpī — to promote intellect, memory and life. Names only; no preparations or doses recorded.

name: Virilization (vājīkaraṇa)
method_summary: The branch that restores potency and fertility for the continuity of lineage. Summary only: no formulations recorded.

warnings.text: Virilization applied to an unpurified body is fruitless.

prerequisites: purification of the body (AHS Utt 39.4 extends the dirty-cloth warning to it)

name: The five purificatory therapies (pañcakarma)
method_summary: After oleation and sudation, the doṣas are expelled by emesis (kapha), purgation (pitta), decoction and oil enemas (vāta) and nasal evacuation (head); then a graded diet. Summary only.

warnings.text: A strong medicine given without examination to a weak patient can kill him; a weak one to a strong patient is useless.
Strong purgative, cauterizing and surgical measures cannot be borne by the weak and may take life at once.

prerequisites: examination of the patient's strength (Ca Vi 8.94)

name: Bloodletting (raktamokṣaṇa)
method_summary: Removal of vitiated blood, counted among the purificatory measures by the surgical school (with leeches, venesection and the like). RESTRICTED: summary only; no method recorded.

warnings.text: Venesection belongs to the surgeon's domain (Dhānvantarīyas); Caraka refers such procedures to them.

notes: Suśruta chapter refs recalled (Sū 13 leeches, Śā 8 venesection), not checked.

name: Collyrium (añjana)
method_summary: Daily application of collyrium to the eyes, which are of the nature of fire and threatened by kapha (AHS Sū 2.5-6).

name: Daily nasal oil (nasya / pratimarśa)
method_summary: Oil in the nose as part of the daily routine, for the head and senses (AHS Sū 2.6; Ca Sū 5).

name: Gargling and holding liquid in the mouth (gaṇḍūṣa, kavala)
method_summary: Holding oil or decoctions in the mouth as part of the daily routine (AHS Sū 2.6; Ca Sū 5).

name: Conquest of the mind (sattvāvajaya)
method_summary: Restraining the mind from unwholesome objects; for mental disorder, examining with understanding what is wholesome in dharma, artha and kāma, serving those who know, and cultivating knowledge of self, place, family, time and strength; knowledge, understanding, steadiness, memory and concentration are the medicines of the mind.

name: Therapy resting on the divine (daivavyapāśraya)
method_summary: Mantra, wearing of herbs and gems, auspicious rites, offerings, gifts, oblations, observances, expiation, fasting, benedictions, prostration and pilgrimage, used especially for karma-born and exogenous disorders. No mantras or rites recorded.

name: Caraka's means to liberation
method_summary: Serving the good and avoiding the wicked; vows, fasts and restraints; study of the dharma treatises; delight in solitude and aversion to objects; approaching a teacher; renunciation of possessions (the renunciant's requisites); acting with mindfulness in all movements; bearing opposites; withdrawing the senses into the mind and the mind into the self; counting the body's parts by dhātus; contemplating all that is caused as suffering, not one's own and impermanent; all flowing from the recollection of truth (tattvasmṛti), culminating in the understanding 'this is not I, not mine' and final renunciation.
signs_of_progress: purified mind shining like a polished mirror or a lamp in a windless place (Śā 5.13-15)

equivalents.note: mindfulness in all postures and activities and contemplation of the body's parts

name: Initiation of the medical student
method_summary: At an auspicious time the fasting, bathed, ochre-clad student brings the requisites; the teacher kindles the fire, offers to Brahmā, Agni, Dhanvantari, Prajāpati, the Aśvins, Indra and the sages, and before fire, brahmins and physicians instructs him in the vows (celibacy, truth, no meat, no weapons, obedience, service of all beings, never harming the sick); the student assents. Mantras not recorded.

name: The processing of mercury (rasa-saṃskāra)
method_summary: The rasa texts require mercury to be purified of its natural and adventitious impurities and brought through a series of eighteen processings before any use, under a qualified guru, in a proper hall. RESTRICTED: the processes, ingredients, apparatus and quantities are deliberately not recorded.

warnings.text: Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.
Impure minerals and metals destroy life (impure pyrite causes death without doubt; impure copper and iron destroy life, strength and lustre).
Mercury is not to be used where a vital point is injured or in burns from caustic or fire.
Without the guru's grace and permission the work is fruitless; the unfit gain nothing and lose their wealth.

name: Metal transmutation (lohavedha / dhātuvāda)
method_summary: The transformation of base metals by processed mercury, treated in the 'vāda' sections of the rasa texts and regarded as a test to be passed before mercury is applied to the body. RESTRICTED: summary only.

warnings.text: Rasa-śāstra is not to be taken as merely for metallurgy; its purpose is liberation through the body.
Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.

name: Transformation of the body (dehavedha)
method_summary: The application of perfected mercury to the body to make it stable, ageless and 'divine' as the basis for yoga and liberation in life — first tested on metal. RESTRICTED: summary and warnings only.

warnings.text: As in metal, so in the body: first test on metal, afterward apply to the body.
Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.
Impure minerals and metals destroy life (impure pyrite causes death without doubt; impure copper and iron destroy life, strength and lustre).
Mercury is not to be used where a vital point is injured or in burns from caustic or fire.
Without the guru's grace and permission the work is fruitless; the unfit gain nothing and lose their wealth.

signs_of_progress: in the texts' claims: freedom from disease, agelessness, sky-going, the powers (Rasahṛdaya 1.3, 1.26) — claims, not endorsements

name: Rejuvenation with metallic and mineral preparations
method_summary: Later Āyurveda and the rasa texts use calcined metals, minerals and mercurial compounds as rejuvenatives and medicines. RESTRICTED: summary only; no preparations or doses.

warnings.text: Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.
Impure minerals and metals destroy life (impure pyrite causes death without doubt; impure copper and iron destroy life, strength and lustre).
Mercury is not to be used where a vital point is injured or in burns from caustic or fire.

name: Worship of the mercurial liṅga
method_summary: Seeing, touching, remembering, worshipping and giving mercury, and worship of a liṅga made of processed mercury, are praised as surpassing all other liṅga worship. RESTRICTED: the making of the liṅga and its rites are not recorded.

warnings.text: Mercury with its impurities, though nectar itself, is poison; a physician skilled in practice but ignorant of the science is death in human form.

name: Initiation into rasa-knowledge
method_summary: Rasa-knowledge is given only by a qualified guru, pleased by the disciple's devotion, after initiation and worship, and kept secret. RESTRICTED: rites and mantras not recorded.

warnings.text: Without the guru's grace and permission the work is fruitless; the unfit gain nothing and lose their wealth.

prerequisites: devotion to the guru, good conduct, initiation (RRS 6.5-6)

name: Breath-holding as the second 'discipline of action' (Rasārṇava)
method_summary: The Rasārṇava pairs mercury with breath: knowledge comes from holding the breath, and the body is stabilized by both. RESTRICTED (breath retention): summary only; no method, counts or durations.
